Lessons.Title: Some Functions Have Symmetry
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Generalize (orally and in writing) what is true for coordinate pairs of even and odd functions. Identify (orally) features that graphs of even functions have in common and features that graphs of odd functions have in common.
An even function satisfies f(-x)=f(x) and has y-axis symmetry. An odd function satisfies f(-x)=-f(x) and has origin symmetry. Both require domains symmetric about zero.

Source activity 5.1: Changing Heights: The table shows Clare’s elevation on a Ferris wheel at different times, \(t\). Clare got on the ride 80 seconds ago. Right now, at time 0 seconds, she is at the top of the ride. Assuming the Ferris wheel moves at a constant speed for the next 80 seconds, complete the table. Practice Problem 1: Classify each function as odd, even, or neither. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 2: The table shows the values of an even function \(f\) for some inputs. Complete the table. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: Here is the graph of \(y = x -2\). Is there a vertical translation of the graph that represents an even function? Explain your reasoning. Is there a vertical translation of the graph that represents an odd function? Explain you reasoning. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: The function \(f\) is odd. Which statements must be true? Select all that apply. If \(f(5) = 2\), then \(f(\text-5) = 2\). If \(f(5) = 3\), then \(f(\text-5) = \text-3\). Reflection over the \(y\)-axis takes the graph of \(f\) to itself. Reflecting \(f\) across both axes takes the graph of \(f\) to itself. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: Find the exact solution(s) to each of these equations, or explain why there is no solution. \(\frac14 \sqrt[3]{d}=15\) \(\text- \sqrt[3]{e}=7\) \(\sqrt[3]{f-5}+2=4\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: Here is the graph of \(f\). Graph the function \(g\) given by \(g(x) = \text-f(x)\). Graph the function \(h\) given by \(h(x) = f(\text-x)\). Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 7: The graph models Priya's heart rate before, during, and after a run. What was Priya's approximate heart rate before and after the run? About how high did Priya's heart rate get during the run? Sketch what the graph would look like if Priya went for the run three hours later. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
